prompt:
Create a third high-fidelity desktop web-app UI concept at 1440×1000 for the same private social Teen Patti product and the same established clubhouse design system shown in the reference image. Preserve the identity exactly in spirit: near-black deep green page (#07110E), rich green felt (#163E2D), warm invitation gold (#E8B04A), warm ivory typography (#F6ECD8), dark lacquer brown rail (#2A1714), elegant high-contrast serif display headings paired with geometric sans-serif UI text, restrained soft shadows, tactile card-room materials, premium adult social atmosphere. This must clearly belong to the same product, but it must use a substantially different operational structure from the reference.

Direction: TABLE LEDGER. Design the authenticated lobby as a refined card-room operating ledger rather than a card-grid dashboard. Use one broad, horizontal “Your private table” scorecard spanning the upper half with table name “Sunday Circle”, room code “ACE-482”, “1 of 6 seated”, “Friends only”, a simple six-seat status strip, and a dominant gold “Share invite” action. Beneath it, show a quiet chronological invitation ledger with three truthful system states only: “Table created”, “Invite ready to share”, and “Waiting for friends”; do not invent users, messages, timestamps, popularity, or activity. Keep a small utility column for “Join with a code” and “Start another table”, visually subordinate and unavailable while the active table is in progress if necessary. Keep compact top navigation: Clubhouse, How to play, Profile. Put “Practice & explore” behind a small secondary disclosure below the core flow; no public table grid. Make the hierarchy feel like a beautifully crafted physical club scorebook fused with a modern web product: crisp alignment, generous spacing, tactile felt and lacquer details, obvious primary action, robust readable labels, board-ready polish. No purchase UI, no fake testimonials, no popularity claims, no real-money language, no casino neon, no gradients, no glassmorphism. The result must look like a credible working web beta screenshot, not a moodboard, wireframe, poster, or marketing landing page.
